title: PaymentReceived.v1
description: Payload of the PaymentReceived event (A§23). Emitted by payment-service — the single producer (A§7.2) — once per distinct payment, whether it arrived from the intraday webhook or from the batch file/CDC path. Payments arrive twice by design (D§47, plan §6.2) and the natural key `(sourceSystem, externalPaymentRef)` absorbs the overlap: the second arrival returns the original payment and publishes nothing, so exactly one PaymentReceived exists per real-world payment. payment-service records the match; it never replaces the bank's authoritative payment system (A§5.10). Published on `collections.payment` keyed by `paymentId` (A§25/§26), immediately followed by the PaymentAllocated for the same payment on the same partition — both enqueued in one transaction through the outbox (SVC-6). Rides the A§24 envelope; a breaking change ships as PaymentReceived.v2 (D§29).

paymentId.description: Platform identifier minted for the payment. Equal to the envelope `aggregateId` and the Kafka partition key (A§26). Stable across redeliveries of the same payment, because the natural key resolves to the same row.

accountId.description: Platform identifier of the account the payment was matched to.

sourceSystem.description: System the payment was reported by. First half of the payment natural key `UNIQUE(sourceSystem, externalPaymentRef)` that makes duplicate intake idempotent (D§47).

externalPaymentRef.description: The source system's own reference for this payment. Second half of the natural key. Source-owned format, never re-minted by the platform and never pattern-constrained here (references legitimately differ per source).

amountMinor.description: Amount received, in minor units of `currency`. Strictly positive: reversals and refunds are separate business facts, never a negative PaymentReceived (a negative amount here would silently corrupt recovery and control totals).

currency.description: ISO-4217 alpha-3 currency of `amountMinor`. Converted to minor units once, by the ingestion canonicalizer, from the source NUMERIC string (D§16, plan §6.8).

receivedAt.description: When the payment was received by the source system (the business fact), RFC3339 UTC with a `Z` offset. Distinct from the envelope `occurredAt`, which is when payment-service recorded the match: for the batch path these can be a day apart, and reconciliation and recovery reporting both key off the business time, not the processing time.

channel.description: How the customer paid. Open SCREAMING_SNAKE vocabulary rather than a closed enum: payment channels are owned by the bank's payment rails and new ones appear without any change in the meaning of this event. Used for recovery attribution and cost-to-collect analysis (D§11).
